Brian Lara, born in Santa Cruz, Trinidad, in 1969, was one of the greatest batsmen in cricket. He played for the West Indies from 1990 to 2007 and was often its captain.

In 1994 he scored 375 against England in Antigua, passing the Test record of Garfield Sobers, and weeks later 501 not out for Warwickshire, the highest first-class score. In 2004 he made 400 not out against England, again in Antigua, which is still the Test record.

He played when the West Indies team was declining after the great years of Viv Richards. The national cricket academy in Trinidad bears his name.
